relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: The temple clock is tied to liberation from Egypt, testing whether sacred building remembers freedom.
Royal measurements give the house a bounded human form.
A porch opens the sanctuary toward those who approach.
Recessed windows allow light without making the holy place transparent.
Chambers gather around sanctuary walls, joining storage and service to worship.
Careful ledges protect the central walls from structural piercing.
The finished site receives prepared stones in silence, while the quarry holds the unremembered noise.
A winding ascent connects the layered chambers.
Cedar closes and shelters the structure.
The side rooms rest against the house through timber drawn from Lebanon.
In the middle of building, a word interrupts the architecture.
The house matters only if the king practices commands and justice.
Divine dwelling is promised among people, not imprisoned inside stone and gold.
Solomon completes the outer task.
Wood covers the interior from floor to ceiling.
The innermost room is set apart within the larger house.
A longer outer hall prepares approach to the inner sanctuary.
Gourds and flowers turn the hidden interior toward living creation.
The inner space is prepared for the covenant ark.
A perfect cube is covered with gold, a human attempt to shape overwhelming holiness.
Gold chains mark a boundary before the inner place.
Splendor spreads over house and altar.
Two olivewood cherubim rise inside the sanctuary.
One creature's wings span the room.
The second mirrors the first in measure.
Their equal height creates balanced guardianship.
Their wings touch walls and one another, joining the entire inner chamber.
Gold covers the carved living forms.
Cherubim, palms, and flowers place a symbolic garden upon every wall.
Even the floor becomes gold beneath human feet.
Olivewood doors define passage into the deepest room.
The doors carry the same garden-throne imagery.
A second olivewood frame marks the temple entrance.
Folding cypress doors regulate movement and sight.
Gold follows the carved forms rather than erasing them.
Stone and cedar shape the inner court where community and sanctuary meet.
The foundation is remembered by month and year.
Seven years of labor disappear into one sentence of completion.

contemplative_note: The house is most sacred where the text refuses to let architecture replace ethics. Divine presence remains among people and answers to practiced justice; the gold is never more holy than the workers, forests, stones, and communities from which it came.
